policy: All actual requested material parts required; omission/abstention partial, contradiction incorrect. Accept semantic equivalents. Evidence within the same response can itself supply a fact or introduce a contradiction, but a bare section name supplies no omitted fact. Distinguish unasked key background from requested procedures, states or outcomes. No cross-answer borrowing.

requested_omissions: Shuffle each tier separately: shuffle all four Conflict III cards, randomly deal five from the shuffled nine Conflict II cards, and randomly deal one from the shuffled three Conflict I cards. Neither the answer nor its evidence supplies shuffling or random selection. Merely specifying five of nine and one of three does not state how those cards are selected, and the III tier also needs a randomized order.
Place the constructed tiers face down. Neither the answer nor its evidence states this required initial card state.

evidence.text: Build the 10-card deck with all 4 Conflict III cards on the bottom, 5 of 9 Conflict II cards above them, and 1 of 3 Conflict I cards on top; return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking.
evidence.finding: Correct counts, tier order, total and unused-card disposition; omits randomization and face-down placement.

evidence.text: Setup, step 2: ‘1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom’; unused cards return ‘without looking.’
evidence.finding: The cited excerpt supplies no additional construction procedure or initial card state; the section reference cannot import its unquoted contents.

evidence.text: Shuffle the four Conflict III cards and place all of them face down in the marked area of the board. Shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five face down on top. Shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one face down on top.

evidence.text: Shuffle the four Conflict III cards and place all of them face down ... Shuffle the nine Conflict II cards, then deal five face down on top ... Shuffle the three Conflict I cards, then deal one face down on top ... Return the unused Conflict cards to the game box without looking at them.

cases.scope_rationale: The question explicitly asks how the deck is built, so randomization is a requested material procedure, not incidental key background: fixed choices or a fixed III order would produce a different deck. Face-down placement is likewise a material initial state of that construction, confirmed by the authoritative source even though the concise key does not spell it out. Tier separation is semantically conveyed by the three tier-specific quantities and ordering and need not be repeated as a separate action. The answer fully handles unused cards and correctly gives all counts and tier positions. No assertion contradicts the rules, so the omissions warrant partial rather than incorrect. The support label and bare reference to Setup step 2 do not fill the missing facts.
